name: WS Audiology
desc: Hearing aid maker selling Widex, Signia and Rexton devices plus hearing-care retail services in over 125 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.63bn in fiscal 2023-24
markets: More than 125 countries; dual headquarters in Lynge, Denmark and Singapore; US retail via HearUSA and TruHearing.
rationale: Consumer hearing brands Signia and Widex target older affluent audiences that match F1's broadcast demographics in Europe and the US.

name: Engel & Völkers
desc: Premium residential and commercial real estate brokerage network with more than 1,000 locations in over 35 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.24bn in 2024
markets: More than 35 countries across Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia, with over 1,000 shop locations.
rationale: Luxury property brand already uses polo for affluent audiences; F1 hospitality in Monaco, Miami and Abu Dhabi reaches the same buyers.

name: Etraveli Group
desc: Online travel group selling flights through Gotogate, Mytrip, Flightnetwork and Flygresor.se in more than 75 markets.
ownership: private equity: CVC Capital Partners (KKR significant minority)
capacity_detail: KKR minority stake valued the company at about EUR 2.7bn (July 2025); revenue EUR 880M in 2025
markets: More than 75 markets, including France, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Canada, Germany, the UK and the US.
rationale: Consumer travel brands Mytrip and Gotogate need mass awareness in Europe and North America, where F1 travel demand is high.

name: Zentiva
desc: Generic and over-the-counter medicines maker with factories in Prague, Bucharest and Ankleshwar, India.
ownership: private equity: GTCR (bought from Advent International, April 2026)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.57bn in 2024
markets: Europe, especially Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, Hungary, Romania, Turkey and the UK, plus manufacturing in India.
rationale: OTC consumer health brands across Central and Eastern Europe could use F1 for pan-European visibility under new ownership.

name: STADA
desc: Pharmaceutical company making generic medicines and consumer health products sold in about 120 countries.
ownership: private equity: CapVest Partners (control agreed Sept 2025, from Bain Capital and Cinven)
capacity_detail: CapVest agreed to buy control in Sept 2025 in a deal valuing Stada at about EUR 10bn; revenue EUR 3.79bn in 2022
markets: About 120 countries, with a strong base in Germany and wider Europe.
rationale: Consumer health brands sold across Europe could use F1's pan-European audience, as rival consumer-goods groups already do.

name: Rodenstock
desc: German maker of ophthalmic spectacle lenses and eyeglass frames, represented in more than 85 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 512.4M in 2024
markets: More than 85 countries, with production in Germany, Czech Republic, Thailand and other sites.
rationale: Premium lens brand competing with EssilorLuxottica, whose Ray-Ban and Oakley are already in F1, could use the sport for vision-and-precision messaging.

name: Belle International
desc: Chinese footwear company owning women's shoe brands Staccato and Millie's and distributing global sportswear brands.
ownership: private equity: Hillhouse Capital and CDH Investments
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.5bn in 2009; taken private for USD 6.8bn in 2017
markets: Mainland China, with stores in Hong Kong and Macau.
rationale: Large Chinese fashion retailer could use F1's Shanghai race and growing Chinese fan base to lift its own shoe brands.

name: Versuni
desc: Household appliance maker selling Philips-licensed, Gaggia, Saeco, Senseo and Preethi kitchen and home appliances.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.2bn in 2021; bought for EUR 3.7bn in 2021
markets: Europe, India (manufacturing in Ahmedabad) and other international markets for Philips-branded home appliances.
rationale: Consumer appliance and coffee-machine brands such as Gaggia and Saeco fit F1 hospitality and global household-name marketing.

name: Element Materials Technology
desc: Testing, inspection and certification company providing materials and product testing services to industries worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 913.0M in 2021; Temasek deal valued at USD 7bn (January 2022)
markets: Worldwide testing laboratories, including the UK and North America.
rationale: Tests aerospace and automotive materials; an F1 technical partnership would showcase engineering credentials to industrial clients.

name: TreeHouse Foods
desc: Manufacturer of private-label packaged foods and beverages for grocery retailers, taken private in February 2026.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 3.45bn in 2023; take-private deal valued at nearly USD 1.2bn, closed February 2026
markets: Mainly the United States, supplying store-brand foods to grocery chains.
rationale: Low fit as a private-label supplier, but Investindustrial ownership and US scale could support B2B hospitality around US Grands Prix.

name: Parexel
desc: Contract research organisation running clinical trials and drug-development services for pharmaceutical and biotech companies.
ownership: private equity: EQT and Goldman Sachs
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2.3bn in 2017; bought for USD 8.5bn in November 2021
markets: Operations in about 100 countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B life-sciences services firm could use F1 hospitality to court pharma clients; brand-led benefit is limited.

name: Stock Spirits
desc: Spirits producer owning more than 70 brands including Żołądkowa Gorzka, Božkov, Stock 84 and Keglevich vodka.
capacity_detail: Revenue about EUR 800M in 2024
markets: Over 50 countries, led by Poland, Czech Republic, Italy and Slovakia, and including the US and Canada.
rationale: Spirits brands competing with F1 partners Chivas, Glenfiddich and Jack Daniel's could use the sport in Central Europe.

name: Universidad Europea
desc: Private university group with campuses in Madrid, Valencia and the Canary Islands, teaching more than 16,000 students.
ownership: private equity: EQT Infrastructure (majority) with Permira (minority)
capacity_detail: EQT bought a majority stake from Permira in 2024 at a valuation of over EUR 2bn
markets: Spain: Madrid (Villaviciosa de Odón and Alcobendas), Valencia and the Canary Islands.
rationale: Its Spanish and international student recruitment could use F1's Madrid Grand Prix from 2026 for brand visibility.

name: Namecheap
desc: Domain name registrar and web hosting provider serving nearly 11 million customers and managing over 10 million domains.
capacity_detail: CVC bought a majority stake in September 2025, valuing the company at USD 1.5bn
markets: Online customers worldwide; nearly 11 million customers as of 2022.
rationale: Consumer-facing web brand competing with GoDaddy and Squarespace could use F1's global digital audience to win small-business customers.

name: Smiths Detection
desc: Maker of threat-detection and security-screening equipment for airports, ports, borders and defence customers.
capacity_detail: Sold by Smiths Group to CVC for GBP 2bn (about USD 2.6bn); completed June 2026
markets: Airports, ports and border agencies worldwide.
rationale: Now independent and B2B; F1 hospitality could reach airport and government buyers, but consumer brand value is limited.

name: TMF Group
desc: Provides corporate secretarial, accounting, payroll and fund administration services through 125 offices in 86 jurisdictions.
ownership: private equity: CVC Capital Partners (about 50%) with ADIA (about 50%)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 744M in 2022
markets: 125 offices across 86 jurisdictions in Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Serves multinationals in many F1 host countries; hospitality could support business development, though brand awareness need is modest.

name: Perficient
desc: Digital consultancy providing technology implementation, data and AI services, with delivery centres across Latin America, Europe and India.
capacity_detail: Acquired by EQT in a USD 3bn all-cash deal agreed May 2024, completed October 2024
markets: North America, with offices in Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Uruguay, India, Serbia, Romania and the UK.
rationale: IT services rivals such as Cognizant, Globant and DXC already use F1 to win enterprise clients; Perficient could follow.

name: Odido
desc: Dutch mobile and broadband operator, formerly T-Mobile Netherlands, serving about 6.9 million customers.
ownership: private equity: Apax Partners and Warburg Pincus (50/50)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.31bn in 2024
markets: The Netherlands.
rationale: Consumer telecom brand in Max Verstappen's home market could use F1 and the Dutch fan base for brand building.

name: CeramTec
desc: Maker of advanced technical ceramics and ceramic components for medical implants, industry and electronics.
ownership: private equity: BC Partners (50%) and CPP Investments (50%)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 685M in 2025
markets: Production in Germany, the UK and Switzerland, with sales offices in major markets worldwide.
rationale: Advanced-materials engineering story could suit an F1 technical supplier deal, though it has no consumer brand.

name: TK Elevator
desc: Elevator and escalator manufacturer and service provider with more than 50,000 employees and about 1,000 locations.
ownership: private equity: Advent International and Cinven (with RAG-Stiftung); Kone agreed to buy it in April 2026
capacity_detail: Annual revenue EUR 9.3bn in 2023/24; Kone agreed in April 2026 to buy it for EUR 29.4bn including debt
markets: Sales and service network worldwide; plants in Brazil, Italy, China, Germany, Spain, India, South Korea, Netherlands and the US.
rationale: Global B2B engineering brand could use F1 hospitality with property developers, though the pending Kone takeover clouds any deal.

name: Apleona
desc: Facility and real-estate services provider operating buildings for corporate and public clients across about 30 countries.
ownership: private equity: Bain Capital (bought from PAI Partners, February 2025)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 4bn in 2024
markets: Germany and about 29 other countries across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, including the UAE and Egypt.
rationale: B2B facility services rival to ISS and Sodexo; F1 hospitality could support corporate client relationships across Europe and the Gulf.

name: Neuraxpharm
desc: Pharmaceutical company specialising in medicines for central nervous system disorders, with headquarters in Langenfeld and Barcelona.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 450M in 2021
markets: Germany, Spain and other European countries.
rationale: Prescription pharma with little consumer branding; F1 fit is weak beyond corporate hospitality.

name: Parques Reunidos
industry: theme parks and leisure parks operator
desc: Leisure park operator running over 60 theme parks, water parks and zoos in nine European countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue exceeding USD 570M (year not stated on page)
markets: Spain, Belgium, Norway, Netherlands, Denmark, UK, Germany, France and Italy.
rationale: Family leisure brand in Spain and Europe could tie in with the Madrid Grand Prix and F1's young family audience.

name: Labeyrie Fine Foods
desc: French premium food group making smoked salmon, foie gras and blinis under Labeyrie, Blini, Delpierre and other brands.
ownership: private equity: PAI Partners with co-operative Lur Berri (together 91.25%)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1bn in 2020-21
markets: France and other European markets.
rationale: Premium food brands suit F1 hospitality catering, though the business is mostly French and Europe-focused.

name: Ecotone
desc: European organic and plant-based food group owning sixteen brands including Bjorg, Clipper Tea, Bonneterre and Alter Eco.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 693M in 2022
markets: Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Italy.
rationale: Organic food brands target health-conscious consumers; F1 sustainability messaging could fit, but the brands are mainly European.

name: Vitamin Well
desc: Swedish maker of Vitamin Well drinks, NOCCO energy drinks and Barebells protein bars sold in more than 40 markets.
ownership: private equity: Cinven (largest stake), Bridgepoint (significant minority)
capacity_detail: Cinven's majority-stake deal (August 2024) valued the company at nearly EUR 3bn (USD 3.3bn)
markets: More than 40 markets internationally, led by the Nordics and wider Europe.
rationale: Energy-drink and protein-bar brands compete with F1 partners Monster, Red Bull and Celsius; F1 would accelerate NOCCO and Barebells abroad.

name: BestSecret
desc: Members-only online fashion retailer selling discounted designer and premium brands across 28 European countries.
ownership: private equity: Permira (about 80%), with founders and management
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.415bn in 2024 (more than EUR 1.5bn in 2025)
markets: 28 European countries, led by Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with stores in Munich and Vienna.
rationale: Premium fashion e-commerce brand expanding beyond DACH; F1's affluent European audience matches its designer-brand member base.

name: Restaurant Brands Europe
desc: Operates Burger King, Popeyes and Tim Hortons restaurants in Spain, Portugal, Gibraltar and Andorra, expanding into Italy.
ownership: private equity: Cinven (79%), with founders and RBI; Nov 2026 reports of a sale of Cinven's stake
capacity_detail: Enterprise valuation including debt above EUR 3bn reported June 2026; adjusted EBITDA EUR 210M in 2024
markets: Spain, Portugal, Gibraltar and Andorra, with Popeyes expansion into Italy; 1,058 own restaurants in Q1 2025.
rationale: Mass-market fast-food brands in Spain could activate around the Madrid Grand Prix, as McDonald's franchisee Arcos Dorados does in F1.

name: Osstem Implant
desc: Korean dental implant maker selling implants and dental equipment in about 100 countries, delisted in 2023.
ownership: private equity: MBK Partners and Unison Capital Korea (UCK) consortium
capacity_detail: Sales KRW 1.208 trillion in 2023 (65.8% overseas); 2.5 trillion KRW buyout
markets: About 100 countries; overseas sales were 65.8% of the total in 2023.
rationale: Global dental brand selling to clinicians in about 100 countries could use F1 for precision-engineering positioning and dealer hospitality.

name: Areas
desc: Travel hospitality operator running over 2,200 restaurants and shops in airports, railway stations and motorways in 11 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.264bn in 2025; EUR 2.7bn expected in 2026
markets: 11 countries in Europe and the Americas; the USA is its largest market (28% of revenue, 27 airports).
rationale: Serves 350 million travellers a year at airports; F1 travel-themed activations could lift its consumer-facing dining brands in Europe and the US.

name: Anaqua
desc: US software company providing intellectual property management software and services to corporations and law firms.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Nordic Capital in 2025 for about USD 3bn
markets: Corporate and law-firm clients, based in the United States.
rationale: Niche B2B software; F1 hospitality could reach corporate legal and R&D leaders, but brand-awareness value is low.

name: Coller Capital
desc: Investment manager specialising in buying secondary stakes in private equity and private credit funds from investors.
capacity_detail: Acquired by EQT for up to USD 3.7bn (USD 3.2bn base plus up to USD 500M contingent); completed August 2026
markets: Institutional investors worldwide.
rationale: Now part of EQT; F1 hospitality could serve investor relations, but as an EQT unit it is unlikely to sponsor independently.

name: Interpath
desc: Advisory firm providing restructuring, insolvency, forensic and transaction services, acquired by Bridgepoint from H.I.G. Capital.
capacity_detail: Bridgepoint acquisition from H.I.G. Capital in January 2026 valued the company at GBP 800M
markets: United Kingdom and international offices.
rationale: Professional-services rivals such as Deloitte and PwC use F1 for client hospitality; Interpath could follow at smaller scale.
